findings.title: A sealed managed child can silently become unmanaged when all lifecycle files disappear
findings.evidence: When external-run.json, external-end.json and external-evidence.json are all absent, _reservation returns None and _external_state returns an empty bindings object. suite_status compares only newly derived binding keys, so it never checks the existing completion's managed external_* hash field set. An unchanged final/no-final outcome and unchanged completion hash can therefore satisfy an already sealed accounting record despite complete loss of the canonical lifecycle artifacts.

trusted_reproductions.case: Completed model-no-final child in a sealed two-target suite; then delete all three lifecycle files in the temporary fixture
Observation-backed accepted-final child in a sealed two-target suite; then delete all three lifecycle files in the temporary fixture

findings.impact: This breaks the promised actual-evidence retention/drift seal even after accounting.json exists. It does not change the checked mathematical final itself or demonstrate a sandbox escape; the issue is silently validating missing managed collection evidence as legacy unmanaged data.
findings.required_resolution: Validate the managed lifecycle field set in both directions: a completion carrying managed bindings must require the corresponding valid reservation/evidence/end state, and current managed state must require the exact managed completion fields, including nullable fields where permitted. Preserve genuine old unmanaged archives without treating a managed completion as legacy. Add regressions before and after suite sealing for complete file loss and nullable managed-field deletion.

findings.title: Read-only unclosed suite status does not validate an existing external record chain
findings.evidence: The unclosed-child branch returns unfinished after history/session checks without calling _external_state. This skips reservation/end/evidence validation even when an end exists and requires canonical evidence. The contract's rule that an unclosed child remains unfinished does not waive fail-closed evidence-chain validation.

trusted_reproduction.case: Reserve and validly end an open first child; delete its canonical external-evidence.json; call suite_status without finish

findings.impact: Read-only accounting hides a corrupt/missing ended evidence chain until an explicit close or another validating operation. It must not infer terminal failure or liveness, but it still must refuse invalid evidence.
findings.required_resolution: Validate any present external chain before returning unfinished. Keep valid unended/partial collections unfinished and do not close or derive a terminal outcome during read-only status. Add absent/corrupt end-backed evidence and orphan-chain read-only regressions.

findings.title: Malformed arguments can mask a replayed call identity as model protocol failure
findings.evidence: run checks seen_calls only after function_call returns. function_call can raise ModelStop while parsing arguments first. A single correctly named call with a fresh response ID, a repeated call_id and malformed argument JSON therefore takes the completed/model-protocol-error path instead of the contract's infrastructure/provider-identity path.

trusted_reproduction.case: One successful mocked check, then a fresh response ID with the first call_id replayed and arguments='not JSON'

findings.impact: No second tool dispatch occurs, but a provider identity-integrity failure becomes a model no-final/protocol outcome, reintroducing the wrong side of the model-versus-infrastructure accounting boundary for overlapping errors.
findings.required_resolution: For the selected well-formed function-call identity, enforce missing/replayed call-ID rejection before argument-content classification. Add this combined-fault regression; preserve the declared model-protocol behavior for fresh identities with bad arguments and the no-extra-call policy.
